title: Hyperscalers can't win with investors as they spend big on AI
excerpt: Investors fear AI is following the dot-com playbook, with massive infrastructure spending and uncertain returns raising bubble concerns.
content_html:
By William Edwards

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

When Alphabet revised up its 2026 AI spending projections by $15 billion to $190 billion-$205 billion in its earnings report last Wednesday, investors were quick to show their displeasure. Shares of Alphabet fell as much as 7.4% in trading on Thursday.

It was the latest sign that the market is increasingly skeptical that the heaps of cash hyperscalers are throwing at the AI buildout will see a payoff anytime soon.

Investors worry that they're watching a replay of the dot-com bubble, when companies spent big on internet infrastructure, only to see poor initial returns, leading to a crash in stock prices. They recently cheered on Meta after reports that the company is planning on leasing out its spare cloud capacity — cashing in on all the demand — sending its shares soaring as much as 21% in a matter of days.

So, should hyperscalers follow the collective wisdom of the market and slow their spending plans?

Last Thursday, as Alphabet's stock was getting pummeled, I posed the question to Molly Pieroni, the president at Yacktman Asset Management, which invests in Alphabet.

Her answer was a resounding no — an interesting contrast to the prevailing narrative at the moment, coming from someone who has skin in the game.

"We always like discipline, but in this case, you're really needing to compete to come out the other end in a spot where you want to be," Pieroni said. "So we're not telling them that they need to pull back on capex and invest less."

It highlights the Catch-22 dynamic facing hyperscalers right now. If they pull back on spending, investors might reward them in the short term. But in the long run, they may lose the AI race, while also upsetting investors like Pieroni who think all the spending is justified.

In one sense, investors are right to demand financial discipline from companies they hold. But they also may be overreacting to all the spending to a degree. Pieroni pointed out that Google in particular has a healthy balance sheet, and has a fairly diversified business that it can rely on to drive earnings. The company did beat on earnings in Q2, after all.

For now, it seems most hyperscalers are continuing to tune out investors' protests against their spending. We'll get more insight into their thinking when Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon report earnings later this week.

Last week, I also spoke with Brandon Nelson, a top-performing fund manager at Calamos Investments who is continuing to bet on hyperscaler capex beneficiaries, even after investors have dumped them in recent weeks on fears that the spending could stop. He said the nerves in the market right now are likely to be a temporary blip in an ongoing bull market, and that the spending glut would continue.

"1996 through the peak of the stock market in 2000, there were 10 10% corrections in the Nasdaq. Those were not comfortable," he said. "My best guess is we're going through one of those kind of gut checks in the AI infrastructure buildup."

content_html_zh:
作者：William Edwards 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

当 Alphabet 上周三在财报中将 2026 年人工智能支出预测上调 150 亿美元至 1900 亿至 2050 亿美元时，投资者很快就表达了不满。 Alphabet 股价周四交易中下跌 7.4%。

这是市场越来越怀疑超大规模企业投入人工智能建设的大量现金能否很快得到回报的最新迹象。

投资者担心他们正在目睹互联网泡沫的重演，当时公司在互联网基础设施上投入巨资，但最初的回报却很差，导致股价暴跌。 最近，有报道称 Meta 正计划出租其闲置云容量——利用所有需求兑现——导致其股价在几天之内飙升了 21%，他们最近为 Meta 欢呼雀跃。

那么，超大规模企业是否应该遵循市场的集体智慧并放慢支出计划？

上周四，当 Alphabet 的股价遭受重创时，我向投资 Alphabet 的亚克特曼资产管理公司 (Yacktman Asset Management) 总裁莫莉·皮耶罗尼 (Molly Pieroni) 提出了这个问题。

她的回答是响亮的“不”——与目前流行的叙述形成有趣的对比，来自一个参与其中的人。

“我们总是喜欢纪律，但在这种情况下，你真的需要竞争才能到达你想要的位置，”皮罗尼说。 “所以我们并没有告诉他们需要削减资本支出并减少投资。”

它强调了超大规模企业目前面临的第 22 条军规动态。 如果他们削减支出，投资者可能会在短期内奖励他们。 但从长远来看，他们可能会输掉人工智能竞赛，同时也会让像皮耶罗尼这样认为所有支出都是合理的投资者感到不安。

从某种意义上说，投资者要求其持有的公司遵守财务纪律是正确的。 但他们也可能在某种程度上对所有支出反应过度。 皮耶罗尼指出，谷歌尤其拥有健康的资产负债表，并且拥有相当多元化的业务，可以依靠它来推动盈利。 毕竟，该公司第二季度的盈利确实超出了预期。

目前看来，大多数超大规模企业仍在继续忽视投资者对其支出的抗议。 当微软、Meta 和亚马逊本周晚些时候公布财报时，我们将更深入地了解他们的想法。

上周，我还与卡拉莫斯投资公司（Calamos Investments）业绩最佳的基金经理布兰登·尼尔森（Brandon Nelson）进行了交谈，尽管投资者因担心支出可能停止而在最近几周抛售了超大规模资本支出受益者，但他仍继续押注于超大规模资本支出受益者。 他表示，目前市场的紧张情绪可能只是持续牛市中的暂时现象，支出过剩将持续下去。

“从1996年到2000年股市的顶峰，纳斯达克指数出现了10次10​​%的调整。 这些不舒服，”他说。 “我最好的猜测是，我们正在对人工智能基础设施的建设进行一种内部检查。”

William Edwards 是 Business Insider 的高级投资记者，主要报道美国股市和更广泛的经济。他采访了市场上一些最有影响力的声音，包括 Joseph Stiglitz、Jeremy Grantham、Rick Rieder、Rob Arnott、Savita Subramanian、Nouriel Roubini、Ken Rogoff、Mike Wilson、Claudia Sahm、Albert Edwards、Andrew Ross Sorkin、Ben Snider 等。William 推出了 BI 年度报告华尔街先知名单（2023 年、2024 年、2025 年），重点关注策略师、经济学家和分析师的重要呼吁。 他还撰写 BI 的《Where to Invest 10,000 美元》专栏，并为 First Trade 时事通讯撰稿。在加入 Business Insider 之前，William 为华盛顿特区的彭博新闻社报道美国经济，并为旧金山的 CNBC 电视科技报道做出贡献。 他还曾在法国、德国和突尼斯学习或报道。他现居纽约。
